A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MP-SAE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic hierarchy experiments, ImageNet and COCO representation analyses, and TinyStories experiments in Sections 4 and B.1–B.5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds fixed-firing and child-activation-distribution experiments in Appendix B.1.4, Figure 16, and Table 1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same greedy feature selection, coefficient calculation, residual updates, and reconstruction procedure. The explicit shared-dictionary explanation in v2 clarifies tied weights already documented in v1; it does not introduce a component.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1.4 extends synthetic coverage to fixed, perfectly correlated firing magnitudes and varying child activation distributions. ImageNet, COCO, and TinyStories coverage remains unchanged; the Gemma checkpoint mention does not establish an additional evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in retained experiments is unchanged. New Table 1 reuses Vanilla, BatchTopK, and Matryoshka, while the additional fixed-firing illustration uses the existing Vanilla and Matryoshka comparators.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce a cosine-similarity absorption score, a child-mean/variance grid with a fixed parent distribution, and a fixed-firing test reporting 15,000 iterations and threshold T=0.6. These are additional protocols; the retained synthetic experiment still reports the 0.05 stopping threshold and the same Gaussian activation distribution.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1.4 substantially strengthens scrutiny of the central synthetic result by testing whether hierarchy recovery depends on firing-magnitude assumptions. Figure 16 exposes instability under perfectly correlated firings, and Table 1 systematically tests sensitivity to child activation strength and variance, including recovery failures.

E5.justification: v2 reports absorption-score averages over 15 independent runs and four independent runs for the new fixed-firing illustration. The existing ten-run medians and four-run synthetic displays remain unchanged; no increase in repetitions for retained experiments or new confidence intervals is established.

E6.justification: Figure 16 adds unstable MP-SAE recovery under fixed firings. Table 1 adds absorption results, including MP=0.073 versus Matryoshka=0.048 in the 0.5 column and 1/400 row. Existing result plots remain unchanged, but the revised Figure 15 discussion newly reports 2–4 active components instead of the ground-truth 1–2.

T1.justification: Definition 4.1 adds a general probabilistic definition of a hierarchical generative process: child activation requires parent activation, while the parent can activate independently. The existing LRH and conditional-orthogonality definitions, Proposition 3.1, and Appendix C guarantees and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies MP-SAE as promoting, rather than enforcing, conditional orthogonality. This narrowly weakens the stated property; the main contributions concerning hierarchical and nonlinearly accessible features, multimodal structure, and adaptive sparsity are retained.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1.4 adds an argument that correlated firing magnitudes favor absorption and explains complementary operating regimes for MP-SAE and Matryoshka. The high-correlation discussion also replaces the single-child explanation with anchor/deviation features, four learned sublevels, and increased sparsity.

D1.justification: v2 documents settings for the added synthetic tests, clarifies averaging of inference-time Babel scores, and adds access information for an advertised Gemma-trained MP-SAE checkpoint. Most rewritten synthetic-generation and training details were already present in v1.

R1.justification: Section 3 replaces the hierarchical-compositional-model reference by Kortylewski et al. with Peotta and Vandergheynst on matching pursuit with block-incoherent dictionaries. v2 also adds Ayonrinde et al. on interpretability as compression and more explicitly positions its synthetic generator relative to Bussmann et al.

P1.justification: v2 locally revises method and multimodal explanations, reorganizes Appendix B.1 into dataset-generation, training, and results subsections, and updates author and publication information. The overall narrative remains intact, although B.1.2 introduces an unremoved drafting note.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 16 and Table 1, updates Figure 3 artwork and its caption, and relocates several retained figures, including Figure 4 into the synthetic-results discussion. Existing experimental plots are preserved; Table 1's caption reverses the displayed row/column descriptions.

improvement.justification: The added fixed-firing control and activation-distribution sweep make the synthetic evidence more informative by exposing MP-SAE's instability and a setting favoring Matryoshka. Clearer discussion of benchmark assumptions and increased sparsity also improves interpretation. These focused gains outweigh minor new editorial defects, including the drafting note and Table 1 caption error.
